verdicts.trueWording: Even if multiple generations have the same reward, shifting all probability to only one of them is an optimal solution.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF arXiv:2501.18101v4 (22pp, pypdf text). Quote verbatim in Sec. 2 'The Alignment Collapse Problem'; preceded by the RL loss L = -sum r_t = -R, so 'optimal solution to the reinforcement-learning objective' is supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Adapting the sampling temperature does not alleviate this problem, as we see a sharp decline in quality.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote verbatim in Sec. 4.1 Results (persona task), pointing to Appendix Figure 11. Both limbs (no alleviation; sharp quality decline) on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: the Llama 3.1 model generates the name “Astrid” more than 10% of the time
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote verbatim in Sec. 4.1 Results, sentence opens 'As shown in Figure 2'; the model under test is named two sentences earlier as Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct.

verdicts.trueWording: Compared to DPO, DivPO with ρ = 0.3 is 74.6% more diverse, with only a drop of 6.4% in quality.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote verbatim in Sec. 4.2 Results; section heading is '4.2 Keyword Story Generation Task' and the abstract calls the same number 'a 74.6% increase in story diversity'. The 6.4% quality drop limb is in the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: standard state-of-the-art models such as Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct and GPT-4o fail to produce diverse personas
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote verbatim in Sec. 4.1 Results, with GPT-4o named in the same sentence and Table 1 cited.

verdicts.trueWording: feedback on text passages given by AI assistants does not depend solely on the content of the text but is affected by the user's preferences
verdicts.note: Raw PDF arXiv:2310.13548v4 (35pp). Quote verbatim in Sec. 3.1, whose opening sentence says the user asks for 'free-form feedback on a passage of text', supporting the free-form limb.

verdicts.trueWording: models tend to admit mistakes even when they didn't make a mistake—Claude 1.3 wrongly admits mistakes on 98% of questions
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote verbatim in Sec. 3.2 'AI assistants can be easily swayed', whose setup is the user challenging the answer ('Are you sure?').

verdicts.trueWording: This model learns that matching a user's views is one of the most predictive features of human preference judgments
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote verbatim in Sec. 1, summarising Sec. 4.1; the same passage names the analysed data as the hh-rlhf dataset (Bai et al., 2022a).

verdicts.trueWording: We constructed this 'non-sycophantic' PM by prompting the Claude 2 PM with a human-assistant dialog where the human explicitly asks the assistant for truthful responses.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote fragment verbatim in Sec. 1, summarising Sec. 4.2. The paper's own label is 'non-sycophantic' (its scare quotes); the claim's weaker 'less sycophantic' is entailed, and the truthful-responses dialog limb is explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: indiscriminate use of model-generated content in training causes irreversible defects in the resulting models
verdicts.note: Raw PDF of the Nature version via pure.ed.ac.uk (7pp, HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the abstract.

verdicts.trueWording: In particular, enforcing this for the LLM experiments causes the perplexity to double compared with the original.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote verbatim in 'Ablation: Repetitions'; the same paragraph sets 'a repeating penalty of 2.0' (paper's wording for repetition penalty).

verdicts.trueWording: Models remain as susceptible to model collapse, if not more.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Claim carried no quote, so verbatim grading is not available; the page's sentence in 'Ablation: Repetitions' immediately follows the repeating-penalty-of-2.0 experiment and states the claim almost word for word.

verdicts.trueWording: We fine-tune the OPT-125m causal language model... We fine-tune it on the wikitext2 dataset
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote verbatim in Methods; the immediately preceding sentence names OPT-125m (Meta, via Hugging Face) as the model fine-tuned.

verdicts.trueWording: preservation of the original data allows for better model fine-tuning and leads to only minor degradation of performance
verdicts.note: Raw PDF. Quote verbatim in the Methods ten-epoch bullet: 'Ten epochs, 10% of original training data preserved... with every new generation of training, a random 10% of the original data points is sampled.'

verdicts.trueWording: the base model produces the winning poem in terms of creative originality in all cases
verdicts.note: Raw PDF arXiv 2505.00047 (COLM 2025, West & Potts). Quote verbatim under 'A split between preference and originality'; the eval is described as '12 contests of 15 poems each', 720 Prolific comparisons. Note: that heading sits in Section 4.2 Results, not 4.1 as the claim's page hint says — a locator slip, not a claim defect.
